children.translated_text: Homage to the one lovely with the moon as a fly-whisk kissing his lofty head,
to <s>Śambhu</s>, the root-pillar for the founding of the city of the three worlds.
I bow to <s>Umā</s>, whose eyes are closed in delight at embracing <s>Hara</s>'s neck,
as though she had fallen into a faint produced by contact with the kālakūṭa poison.
Homage to that all-knowing <s>Vyāsa</s>, the creator among poets,

children.text: cakre puṇyaṃ sarasvatyā yo varṣamiva bhāratam ||
children.translated_text: who made the holy <s>Bhārata</s> by <s>Sarasvatī</s>, as if he had made a rain-year.
For the most part bad poets in the world have their sight fixed on passion;
like cuckoos they are born talkative and acting as desire moves them.
There are countless creatures possessing birth in every house, like dogs;

children.text: utpādakā na bahavaḥ kavayaḥ śarabhā iva ||
children.translated_text: but producers, poets, are not many, like śarabhas.
By disguising themselves under another's color and by concealing the signs of bondage,
an unannounced poet-thief is detected among good men.
Among northerners there is mostly paronomasia; among westerners only meaning;
among southerners imaginative supposition; among the Gauḍas a pomp of syllables.
Fresh meaning, a style not vulgar, paronomasia not labored, rasa clearly manifest,
and a compact arrangement of difficult syllables: all this together in one place is hard to achieve.
What use is the poetry of that poet whose <s>Bhāratī</s>,

children.text: katheva bhāratī yasya na vyāpnoti jagattrayam ||
children.translated_text: like a story ranging through every event, does not pervade the three worlds?
Those in whose mouth <s>Sarasvatī</s> is unwearied even at the end of an ucchvāsa,
how could they, makers of narrative prose, not be venerable lords of poets?
Surely the pride of poets melted away because of <s>Vāsavadattā</s>,
as the power of the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s> did when it reached <s>Karṇa</s>'s ear.
Bright with the binding of words, charming, with the ordered placement of letters established,
the prose composition of venerable <s>Hariścandra</s> conducts itself like a king.
<s>Sātavāhana</s> made an imperishable and unvulgar treasury
with sayings of pure kind, like a treasury with jewels.
The fame of <s>Pravarasena</s>, bright as a white lotus, went
to the farther shore of the ocean by means of a bridge, like the army of monkeys.
With plays whose openings were made by stage-managers, with many roles,
and furnished with banners, <s>Bhāsa</s> gained fame, as if with temples of the gods.

children.text: nirgatāsu na vā kasya kālidāsasya sūktiṣu
children.translated_text: When the utterances of <s>Kālidāsa</s> have gone forth, in whom indeed
does dense sweet delight not arise, as in clusters of blossoms?
Kindling <s>Kandarpa</s>, preparing the adornment of <s>Gaurī</s>,
the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s>, like a sport of <s>Hara</s>, is a wonder to whom among us?
Even when remembered, the efforts made by the wealthy king and lodged in the heart
do not set my tongue to poetry, as though it were being pulled inward.
Nevertheless, through devotion to the king, afraid and anxious about completion,
I make the restless motion of launching my tongue upon the ocean of narrative prose.
Easy to understand and graceful, shining with words like bright golden jars,
the narrative shines like a bed with its supporting feet.
Victorious is <s>Harṣa</s>, a mountain of fortune granting the fulfilment of all loving people's desires,
protecting the world with a rampart made from the blazing fire of his burning majesty.

children.text: evamanuśrūyate purā kila bhagavānsvalokamadhitiṣṭhanparameṣṭhī vikāsini pajhaviṣṭhare samupaviṣṭaḥ sunāsīrapramukhairgīrvāṇaiḥ parivṛto brahnodyāḥ kathāḥ kurvannanyāśca niravadyā vidyāgoṣṭhīrbhāvayankadācidāsāñcakre ||
children.translated_text: Thus it is heard: long ago, once, the blessed <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, dwelling in his own world, sat upon a broad blossoming lotus-seat, surrounded by gods headed by <s>Sunāsīra</s>, holding discussions on sacred knowledge and fostering other faultless assemblies of learning.

children.text: tathāsīnaṃ ca taṃ tribhuvanapratīkṣyaṃ manudakṣacākṣuṣaprabhṛtayaḥ prajāpatayaḥ sarve ca saptarṣipuraḥsarā maharṣayaḥ siṣevire ||
children.translated_text: As he sat thus, all the Prajāpatis, beginning with <s>Manu</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>, and the great seers headed by the seven seers, attended upon him, who was awaited by the three worlds.
Some recited Ṛg-verses skilled in praise.
Some recited Yajus-formulas that conveyed reverence.
Some sang Sāmans that were Sāmans of praise.
Others explained mantras that unfolded the procedures and ritual systems of sacrifices.
There, among them, disputes with one another arose, produced by disagreements about knowledge.

children.text: athātiroṣaṇaḥ prakṛtyā mahātapā muniratrestanayastārāpaterbhratā nāmnā durvāsā dvitīyena mandapālanāmnā muninā saha kalahāyamānaḥ sāmagāyankrodhāndho visvaramakarot ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Durvāsas</s>, by nature exceedingly irascible, a great ascetic, son of the sage <s>Atri</s> and brother of the lord of stars, was quarrelling with a second sage named <s>Mandapāla</s>; while singing a Sāman, blinded by anger, he made a discordant sound.

children.text: sarveṣu ca teṣu śāpabhayapratipannamauneṣu muniṣvanyālāpalīlayā cāvadhīrayati kamalasambhave bhagavatī kumārī kiñcidunmuktabālabhāve bhūṣitanavayauvane vayasi vartamānā gṛhītacāmarapracaladbhujalatā pitāmahamupavījayantī nirbhartsanatājanajātarāgābhyāmiva svabhāvāruṇābhyāṃ pādapallavābhyāṃ samudbhāsamānā śiṣyadvayeneva padakramamukhareṇa nūpurayugalena vācālitacaraṇayugalā dharmanagaratoraṇastambhavibhramaṃ bibhrāṇā jaṅghādvitayam salīlamutkalahaṃsa kulakalālāpapralāpini mekhalādāmni vinyastavāmahastakisalayā vidvanmānasanivāsalagnena guṇakalāpenevāṃsāvalambinā brahnāsūtreṇa pavitrīkṛtakāyā bhāsvanmadhyanāyakamanekamuktānuyātamapavargamārgamiva hāramudvahantī vadanapraviṣṭasarvavidyālaktakaraseneva pāṭalena sphuratā daśanacchadena virājamānā saṃkrāntakamalāsanakṛṣṇājinapratimāṃ madhuragītākarṇanāvatīrṇaśaśihariṃṇāmiva kapolasthalīṃ dadhānā tiryaksāvajñanunnamitakabhrūlatā śrotramekaṃ visvaraśravaṇakaluṣitaṃ prakṣālayantīvā pāṅganirgatena locanāśrujalapravāheṇetaraśravaṇena ca vikasitasitasindhu vāramañjarījuṣā hasateva prakaṭitavidyāmadā śrutipraṇayibhiḥ praṇavairiva karṇāvataṃsa kusumamadhukarakulairapāsyamānā sūkṣmavimalena prajñāpratānenevāṃśukenācchāditaśarīrā vāṅmayamiva nirmalaṃ dikṣu daśanajyotsnālokaṃ vikirantī devī sarasvatī śrutvā jahāsa ||
children.translated_text: And while all those sages had fallen silent from fear of a curse, and while <s>Kamalasambhava</s>, in the play of some other conversation, ignored him, the blessed maiden <s>Sarasvati</s> heard and laughed. She was at an age when a little of childhood had just been released and fresh youth adorned her. Holding a yak-tail fan, with the creeper of her arm moving, she fanned her grandsire. She shone with her naturally ruddy foot-shoots, as if flushed by the redness born from the act of rebuke; her pair of feet was made vocal by a pair of anklets, noisy with the succession of their steps, like two pupils. She bore in her two shanks the graceful semblance of the gateway-pillars of the city of <s>dharma</s>. Her left hand, like a tender sprout, rested on the girdle-string, which prattled playfully with the cries of an excited flock of swans. Her body was purified by a <s>brahmasutra</s> hanging from her shoulder, like a cluster of virtues attached to the abode of learned minds. She wore a necklace like the path to liberation, bright with a central leader and followed by many pearls. Her gleaming, rosy lip shone as if reddened by the lac-dye of all the sciences that had entered her mouth. She had cheeks on which the reflected image of <s>Kamalasana</s>'s black antelope skin had passed, as though moon-deer had descended there on hearing her sweet song. With a creeper-like brow raised sideways in disdain, she seemed to wash one ear, sullied by hearing a discordant sound, with the stream of tear-water issuing from the corner of her eye; and with the other ear, graced by a blooming white sindhuvara spray, she displayed, as if laughing, the intoxication of learning. Swarms of bees on the flowers at her ears, like <s>pranavas</s> fond of scripture, hovered about her. Her body was covered by a fine, spotless garment, like a spreading web of intelligence. Scattering in the directions the light of her tooth-moonlight, as if it were pure literature itself, the goddess <s>Sarasvati</s>, having heard, laughed.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tāṃ tathā hasantīṃ sa muniḥ āḥ pāpakāriṇi durgṛhītavidyālavāvalepadurvidagdhe māmupahasasi' ityuktvā śiraḥkampaśīryamāṇabandhaviśarārorunmiṣatpiṅgalimno jaṭākalāpasya rociṣā siñcanniva roṣadahanadraveṇa daśa diśaḥ kṛtakālasannidhānāmivāndhakāritalalāṭapaṭṭāṣṭāpadāmantakāntaḥ puramaṇḍanapatrabhaṅgamakarikāṃ bhrukuṭimāvadhnan atilohitena cakṣuṣāmarṣadevatāyai svarudhiropahāramiva prayacchan nirdayadaṣṭadaśanacchadabhayapalāyamānāmiva vācaṃ rundhandantāṃśucchalena asāvasraṃsinaḥ śāpaśāsanapaṭṭasyeva grathnangranthimanyathā kṛṣṇājinasya svedakamapratibimbitaiḥ śāpaśaṅkāśaraṇāgatariva surāsuramunibhiḥ pratipannasarvāvayavaḥ kopakampataralitāṅgulinā kareṇa prasādanalagnāmakṣaramālāmivākṣamālāmākṣipya kāmaṇḍalavena vāriṇā samupaspṛśya śāpajalaṃ jagrāha ||
children.translated_text: And seeing her laughing in that way, the sage said, 'Ah, wicked woman, badly clever from the arrogance of a mere particle of ill-grasped learning, you mock me!' Having said this, he bound his frown like a makara-shaped leaf ornament on the inner palace of <s>Antaka</s>, darkening the broad golden plate of his forehead as if <s>Kala</s> himself had drawn near. As the knot of his matted hair, loosened and falling apart through the shaking of his head, opened with a tawny glow, he seemed to sprinkle the ten directions with the liquid fire of anger. With eyes exceedingly red he seemed to offer his own blood as an oblation to the deity of wrath. He checked his speech behind the glitter of his teeth, as though the words were fleeing in terror from his mercilessly bitten lip. With the sweat-drops reflected on his slipping black antelope skin, he seemed to be covered in all his limbs by gods, demons, and sages who had come for refuge in fear of the curse. With a hand whose fingers trembled from anger, he flung aside his rosary, as if it were a garland of syllables clinging to him in supplication; then, after sipping water from his water-pot, he took up water for the curse.

children.text: atrāntare svayambhuvo 'bhyāśe samupaviṣṭā devī mūrtimatī pīyūṣaphenapaṭalapāṇḍuraṃ kalpadrumadukūlavalkalaṃ vasānā visatantumayenāṃśukenonnatastanamadhyabaddhagātrikāgranthiḥ tapobalanirjitatribhuvanajayapatākābhiriva tisṛbhirbhasmapuṇḍrakarājibhirvirājitalalāṭājirā skandhāvalambinā sudhāphenadhavalena tapaḥprabhāvakuṇḍalīkṛtena gaṅgāsrītaseva yogapaṭṭakena viracitavaikakṣyakā savyena brahnotpattipuṇḍarīkamukulamiva sphaṭikakamaṇḍaluṃ kareṇa kalayantī dakṣiṇamakṣamālākṛtaparikṣepaṃ kambunirmitormikādanturitaṃ tarjanataraṅgitatarjanīkamutkṣipantī karam āḥ pāpa krodhopahata durātman ajña anātman ajña anātmajña brahnabandho muniśeṭa apasada nirākṛta kathamātmaskhalitavilakṣaḥ surāsuramunimanujavṛndavandanīyāṃ tribhuvanamātaraṃ bhagavatīṃ sarasvatīṃ śaptumabhilaṣasi' ityabhidadhānā roṣavimuktavetrāsanairoṅkāramukharita mukherutkṣepa dolāyamānajaṭābhārabharitadigbhiḥ parikarabandhabhramita kṛṣṇājināṭopacchāyāśyāmāyamānadivasairamarṣaniḥśvāsadolāpreṅkholitabrahnalokaiḥ somarasamiva svedavisaravyājena sravadbhiragnihotrapavitrabhasmasmeralalāṭaiḥ kuśatantucāmaracīracīvaribhirāṣāḍhibhiḥ praharaṇīkṛtakamaṇḍalumaṇḍalairmūrtaiścaturbhirvedaiḥ saha bṛsīmapahāya sāvitrī samuttasthau ||
children.translated_text: At that moment the embodied goddess <s>Savitri</s>, who was seated near <s>Svayambhu</s>, rose from her seat together with the four Vedas embodied. She wore a garment and bark-cloth of wish-fulfilling-tree silk, white as a mass of nectar-foam; over it she had a cloth of lotus-fibers, with the knot of its bodice tied between her high breasts. The courtyard of her forehead was adorned by three rows of ash-marks, like victory banners from her ascetic power's conquest of the three worlds. A yogic strap, white as nectar-foam, hung from her shoulder and formed a single-shoulder band, as though the stream of <s>Ganga</s> had been coiled by the power of her austerity. In her left hand she held a crystal water-pot, like the bud of the lotus from which <s>Brahma</s> was born. She lifted her right hand, encircled by a rosary, roughened with shell-made rings, its forefinger waving like a wave of rebuke, and said: 'Ah, sinner, your anger has destroyed you. Evil-minded one, ignorant one, one who does not know the self, pretended Brahmin, dreg of sages, outcast: how, embarrassed by your own lapse, do you desire to curse the blessed <s>Sarasvati</s>, mother of the three worlds, worthy of veneration by hosts of gods, demons, sages, and men?' With their mouths resounding with <s>om</s> as they left their cane seats in anger, with the mass of their matted hair swaying upward and filling the quarters, with the display of black antelope skins whirled by the fastening of their girdles making the day grow dark, with their angry breaths setting <s>Brahmaloka</s> rocking like a swing, with sweat streaming as if it were soma juice, with foreheads smiling bright with the sacred ash of the agnihotra, wearing garments of kuśa-fiber, bark, and rags, carrying staffs, and making circles of water-pots into weapons, those embodied four Vedas rose with her.

children.text: tato marṣaya bhagavan abhūmireṣā śāpasyetyanunāthyamāno 'pi vibudhaiḥ upādhyāya ||
children.translated_text: Then, though the gods implored him, 'Forbear, lord; she is no proper object for a curse,' the teacher ...

children.text: skhalitamekaṃ kṣamasva' iti baddhāñjalipuṭaiḥ prasādyamāno 'pi svaśiṣyaiḥ putra mā kṛthāstapasaḥ pratyūham' iti nivāryamāṇo 'pyatriṇā roṣāveśavivaśo durvāsāḥ durvinīte! vyapanayāmi te vidyajanitāmunnatimimām adhastādgaccha martyalokam' ityuktvā tacchā podakaṃ visasarja ||
children.translated_text: Though his own pupils, with hollowed hands joined in reverence, tried to propitiate him, saying, "Forgive this one slip," and though <s>Atri</s> tried to stop him, saying, "Son, do not make an obstacle to your asceticism," <s>Durvasas</s>, helpless under the invasion of anger, said, "Ill-behaved woman, I remove this elevation of yours produced by learning. Go down below, to the world of mortals," and released that water of curse.

children.text: pratiśāpadānodyatāṃ sāvitrīm sakhi saṃhara roṣam asaṃskṛtamatayo 'pi jātyaiva dvijanmāno mānanīyāḥ' ityabhidadhānā sarasvatyeva nyavārayat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvati</s> herself restrained <s>Savitri</s>, who was ready to give a counter-curse, saying, "Friend, contain your anger. Even if their minds are uncultivated, twice-born men are by birth itself to be honored."

children.text: atha tāṃ tathā śaptāṃ sarasvatīṃ dṛṣṭvā pitāmaho bhagavānkamalotpattilagnamṛṇālasūtrāmiva dhvalayajñopavītinīṃ tanumudrahan udgacchadacchāṅgulīyamarakatamayūkhalatākalāpena tribhuvanopaplavapraśamakuśāpīḍadhāriṇeva dakṣiṇena kareṇa nivārya śāpakalakalam ativimaladīrghairbhāvikṛtayugārambhasūtrapātamiva dikṣu pātayan daśanakiraṇaiḥ sarasvatīprasthānamaṅgalapaṭaheneva pūrayannāśāḥ svareṇa sudhīramuvāca brahnan na khalu sādhusevito 'yaṃ pantā ||
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Sarasvati</s> cursed in that way, the blessed <s>Pitamaha</s>, wearing a white sacred thread like a lotus-fiber strand attached to the lotus from which he had arisen, raised his body; with his right hand, which was encircled by a cluster of rays from a clear emerald ring rising on his finger and seemed to hold a bunch of kuśa grass for pacifying the disturbance of the three worlds, he checked the tumult of the curse; casting into the directions, with his very pure and long rays of teeth, as it were, the laying down of the first threads for a future Kṛta age, and filling the quarters with his voice as with an auspicious drum for <s>Sarasvati</s>'s departure, he spoke very gravely: "<s>Brahman</s>, this is certainly not a path followed by the good.
It is one upon which you have set out.
This destroys one who is devoted to another's injury.
For the dust raised by the unbridled and far-rushing horses of the senses clouds the vision of those who have not conquered the senses.
How far, after all, does the eye see?

children.text: viśuddhayā hi dhiyā paśyanti kṛtabuddhayaḥ sarvānarthānasataḥ sato vā ||
children.translated_text: The wise, whose understanding has been purified, see all calamities, whether unreal or real, with the intellect.
And this coexistence of <s>dharma</s> and anger in one place is contrary to nature, like that of water and fire.

children.text: ālokamapahāya kathaṃ tamasi nimajjasi! kṣamā hi mūlaṃ sarvatapasās ||
children.translated_text: How, abandoning light, do you sink into darkness? For patience is the root of all asceticism.

children.text: paradoṣadarśanadakṣā dṛṣṭiriva kupitā buddhirna te ātmarāgadoṣaṃ paśyati ||
children.translated_text: Like an eye expert at seeing another's faults, your angry mind does not see the fault of attachment within yourself.

children.text: kva mahāpobhāravaivadhikatā kva purobhāgitvam atiroṣaṇaścakṣuṣmānandha eva janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What connection is there between bearing the burden of great ascetic heat and going in front as a rash aggressor? A person who is excessively angry is blind, though possessed of eyes.

children.text: nahiṃ kopakaluṣitā vimṛśati matiḥ kartavyamakartavyaṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: For a mind muddied by anger does not consider what ought or ought not to be done.
For an angry man, learning first becomes darkened, and then the brow.
At the beginning passion assails the senses; at the end, the eye.
At the start asceticism melts away; afterwards the water of sweat.
First fame quivers; immediately afterward, the lower lip.

children.text: kathaṃ lokavināśāya te viṣapādapasyeva jaṭāvalkalāni jātāni ||
children.translated_text: How have your matted locks and bark garments, like those of a poison-tree, come into being for the destruction of the world?

children.text: anucitā khalvasya muniveṣasya hārayaṣṭiriva vṛttamuktā cittavṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely the condition of your mind is unfitting for this sage's garb, like a necklace whose pearls have fallen from their string.

children.text: śailūṣa iva vṛthā vahasi kṛtrimamupaśamaśūnyena cetasā tāpasākalpam ||
children.translated_text: Like an actor, you carry in vain the costume of an ascetic, artificial and with a heart empty of tranquillity.
I do not see even a little store of merit in you.
Because of this excessive lightness, even now you float only on the surface of the ocean of knowledge.

children.text: na khalvenahamūkā eḍā jaḍā vā sarvaṃ ete maharṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Surely all these great seers are not mute, foolish, or dull.

children.text: roṣadoṣaniṣadye svahṛdaye nigrāhye kimarthamasi nigṛhītavānanāgasāṃ sarasvatīm ||
children.translated_text: When your own heart, the seat of the fault of anger, should have been restrained, why have you restrained the innocent <s>Sarasvati</s>?

children.text: etāni tānyātmapramādaskhalitavailakṣyāṇi yairyāpyatāṃ yātyavidagdho janaḥ' ityuktvā punarāha vatse sarasvati viṣādaṃ mā gāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are those embarrassments caused by slips born from one's own negligence, by which an unskilled man becomes contemptible." Having said this, he spoke again: "Child <s>Sarasvati</s>, do not fall into dejection.
This <s>Savitri</s> will follow you.
And she will comfort you when you are distressed by separation from us.
And this curse of yours will last only until you behold the lotus-face of your son."

Having said only this much, he dismissed the assembly of gods, demons, sages, and men; then, placing his hand on the shoulder of <s>Narada</s>, who had hurriedly approached, he rose to perform the proper daily rite.

children.text: sarasvatyapi śaptā kiñcidadhomukhī dhavalakṛṣṇaśārā kṛṣṇājinalekhāmiva dṛṣṭimurasi pātayantī surabhiniḥ- śvāsaparimalalagnairmūrtaiḥ śāpākṣareriva ṣaṭcaraṇacakrairākṛṣyamāṇā śāpaśokaśithilitahastādhomukhībhūtenopadivyamānamartyalokāvatataraṇamārgevanakhamayūkhajālakena nūpuravyāhārāhūtairbhavanakalahaṃsakulairbrahnalokanivāsihṛdayairivānugamyamānā samaṃ sāvitryā gṛhamagāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvati</s> too, cursed and with her face somewhat lowered, casting upon her breast a glance dark-and-white like a streak of black antelope skin, drawn as if by embodied syllables of the curse in the form of swarms of bees clinging to the fragrance of her fragrant sighs, her hand slackened by grief over the curse, while the net of rays from her downturned nails seemed to point out the path of descent to the mortal world, and followed by flocks of palace swans called by the speech of her anklets as if by the hearts of those dwelling in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, went home together with <s>Savitri</s>.
Meanwhile <s>Amsumalin</s> descended to the middle world, as if to tell the news of <s>Sarasvati</s>'s descent.
